findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Normalise path separators (or add both-separator variants) in the T14 file_impact regex patterns so `.github\workflows\` matches the same as `.github/workflows/` on Windows developer workstations.
evidence: "file_impact (path patterns; declared deletions) evaluated before the text regex"
"exact amended regexes are recorded in the audit on ticket 696a and are transcribed verbatim"
Path patterns listed: `.github/`, `Makefile`, `hooks/`, `*.yml`, `pyproject.toml` — all use forward-slash notation
Windows platform is a named supported venue in the support matrix
findings.finding: The T14 file_impact OR-conditions use forward-slash path patterns (`.github/`, `hooks/`) matched against plan text. On a Windows developer workstation, a plan author may naturally write Windows-style backslash paths (`.github\workflows\ci.yml`). The regex as specified — transcribed verbatim from a Linux-authored audit — uses `/` separators and would silently fail to match, causing T14 to not fire, the criterion to be skipped with zero LLM calls, and a potential missed finding.
findings.location: Approach — "T14 and removal-rationale each carry a structured OR-condition over file_impact (path patterns; declared deletions)"
scenarios: Windows developer workstation: a plan author writes `.github\workflows\deploy.yml` using Windows path separators; the `\.github/` pattern does not match; T14 gate does not fire; criterion is silently skipped; a real CI-impact change goes unreviewed.
findings.suggested_fix: In the gate implementation, normalise the plan's path strings to forward slashes before applying the regex, or use a separator-agnostic pattern such as `[/\\]` at each separator position in the compiled regex.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the error fallback for pre-gate trigger evaluation failure (recommend: fail-open — route to LLM as if triggered — consistent with the existing DET-layer convention at det_invariants.py:55, and record the error in the coverage skip entry).
evidence: Plan: 'a not-fired trigger skips the criterion with an explicit coverage entry recording the skip; a fired trigger routes to the LLM exactly as today' — only two outcomes specified, no error outcome

Existing det_invariants.py:55: `except Exception: logger.warning('could not resolve project DET criteria; skipping')` — existing DET error handling fails open (skips), but plan does not adopt or reference this convention
The new file_impact OR-condition accesses ctx.state['file_impact'] and applies path-glob matching — both can raise on unexpected input types
findings.finding: The plan does not specify a fallback when the pre-gate trigger evaluation itself fails at runtime (e.g., file_impact path-pattern matching raises on malformed state). The existing `overlay_triggers()` only calls `re.search()` on a plain string — which never raises — but the new file_impact arm accesses ticket state dict keys and applies path-glob matching, both of which can fail. The plan says 'a fired trigger routes to the LLM exactly as today' and 'a not-fired trigger skips' but gives no error path.
findings.location: Approach section: 'a not-fired trigger skips the criterion with an explicit coverage entry recording the skip; a fired trigger routes to the LLM exactly as today'; Acceptance Criteria: 'file_impact OR-conditions fire T14 on .github/workflows paths'
scenarios: A ticket with a malformed file_impact field (e.g., non-string entries) causes the OR-condition evaluation to raise; without a specified error path, implementations diverge between fail-open (route to LLM) and fail-closed (skip with error coverage).
Fail-closed on error silently suppresses the criterion for malformed tickets; fail-open on error defeats the pre-gate's purpose for that same class.
